subject: Decision Making
title: Heuristics and Biases
description: A quick win: understand Heuristics and Biases.

hook.text: Your brain uses shortcuts called heuristics. They are fast and usually right but fail in predictable ways.

buildup.text: Availability bias: you judge probability by how easily examples come to mind. Shark attacks feel common; they are rare.

discovery.text: Anchoring: the first number you hear distorts your estimate. A high asking price makes any discount feel reasonable.

twist.text: These biases are not bugs. They are features that work well in most daily situations but fail in complex ones.

climax.text: Knowing your biases does not eliminate them. Awareness helps, but the shortcuts still fire automatically.

punchline.text: Fast, usually right, sometimes wrong. Heuristics are a feature and a flaw.

quiz.question: What is the availability bias?
options: Judging probability by how easily examples come to mind
